The QR findings are thus more disciplined than the OLS picture: dollar dominance across the full distribution is confirmed, but the threshold intensification for BMI, RAC, and inflation is not.

On the digital-asset side, the results tell a proxy story as much as a monetary story. Google Trends adds nothing ($p\_\text{Webb} > 0.40$). The Chainalysis crypto-market premium enters negatively and significantly ($\hat\beta = -0.0082$, $p\_\text{Webb} = 0.045$), suggesting that when domestic buyers absorb a price premium to acquire Bitcoin, some FX pressure is diverted from official markets. The headline result comes from the GCAI triple-interaction test: for Brazil, India, Mexico, and Nigeria, crypto adoption amplifies inflation pass-through ($\hat\beta_{\text{GCAI}\times\pi} = +0.676^{***}$), while Argentina's net interaction is $-10.284^{***}$, driven by its unique combination of binding capital controls, triple-digit inflation, and an active peer-to-peer stablecoin market. Pooling these two regimes produces a pooled coefficient that describes neither.

The conflict in the cryptoization literature is better understood as a measurement dispute than a factual one. Search-based proxies pick up speculative attention; adoption-based proxies are closer to what the substitution theory predicts. And any claim of a general EM absorber effect should be tested for its robustness to the exclusion of individual countries --- in this sample, the absorber disappears when Argentina is removed.

For policymakers, the picture is context-specific. In Argentina-like settings --- binding capital controls, very high inflation, active peer-to-peer stablecoin markets --- stablecoin flows function as an informal dollarisation channel that partially absorbs FX pressure; they are a genuine early-warning indicator of institutional stress [@imf2023_crypto_small_open]. In more open emerging markets, the evidence points toward amplification: crypto adoption deepens rather than dampens currency volatility. And if Argentina were to liberalise its capital account, the informal equilibrium would likely dissolve alongside the restrictions that created it.

One caveat deserves prominence. The baseline crypto premium result ($p\_\text{Webb} = 0.045$) is substantially strengthened by VIX conditioning ($p\_\text{Webb} = 0.001$, 95\% CI: $[-0.0148, -0.0014]$), but the finding still rests on $N = 6$ clusters and 348 observations; the GCAI analysis rests on five clusters and a short verified window. Both findings should be treated as indicative until Chainalysis adoption data extend to more countries and years, and until event-study or on-chain designs can address the identification challenge that panel averages cannot.

---

---

## Highlights

- Webb (2023) wild cluster bootstrap with $B=999$ is applied throughout for panel OLS ($N=6$ clusters)
- Monthly inflation and broad money instability robustly predict EM currency depreciation in panel-OLS specifications ($p_\text{Webb}<0.001$)
- **QR inference corrected (ModC-2)**: pairs cluster bootstrap ($B=399$, resample $N_\text{cl}=6$ with replacement) replaces i.i.d.\ bootstrap; BMI significant only at $\tau=0.50$ (Panel A); RAC not significant at any quantile; DXY significant at all four quantiles (range $+0.38$–$+0.45$); inflation significant at $\tau=0.25$ and $\tau=0.50$ but not in upper tail
- Google Trends attention proxies yield no significant coefficients in any specification ($p_\text{Webb}>0.40$)
- Crypto premium safety-valve result *strengthens* with VIX: $\beta=-0.0081^{***}$ ($p_\text{Webb}=0.001$) — risk-appetite confound ruled out by placebo
- GCAI triple-interaction test: base EM group shows *amplification* ($\hat\beta=+0.676^{***}$); net Argentina absorber effect $-10.284^{***}$ — a contingent equilibrium, not a general EM property

| Nigeria | $+0.443$ | $<0.001$\*\*\* | $-0.943$ | $<0.001$\*\*\* | 114 | 4 |

: {#tbl-loo}

*Notes:* Each row drops the named country from the 2022–2024 GCAI panel and re-estimates the triple-interaction model. When Argentina is dropped, the $AR_i$ triple collapses and only $\hat\beta_5$ is estimated. $\hat\beta_8$ in the Argentina-drop row is therefore not applicable (—). The Mexico result (bold) indicates a sign reversal in $\hat\beta_5$ and loss of significance in $\hat\beta_8$: Mexico is the sole genuinely open-capital-account economy in the sample (KAOPEN = $+1.028$) and provides the primary cross-sectional identification for the amplification regime. Dropping Brazil, India, or Nigeria yields magnitude inflation relative to the full sample, reflecting reduced within-country variation at $N_\text{cl} = 4$. Webb (2023) bootstrap, $B = 999$, seed 2026. \*\*\* $p_\text{Webb} < 0.01$.
